tables.description: Prenatal skin scRNA-seq sample metadata: one row per sample, giving sample ID, donor, gestational age in post-conception weeks and FACS enrichment status. Use it to establish which donors and ages any cell state was observed in.

Overview of every dataset analysed in the study — newly generated and published single-cell and spatial prenatal skin data plus the external datasets used for comparison — with publication, accession codes, technology and per-sample metadata. The place to look up which upstream study a cell state came from.

Differential expression between refined (fine-grained) cell states across the whole prenatal skin scRNA-seq dataset: two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum, Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted. One row per gene per cluster, so this is the primary marker table for any prenatal skin cell state. 139 columns because results are laid out as repeated column blocks.

Milo differential abundance testing: FACS-isolated cell proportions used to correct for sort strategy, then per-neighbourhood differential abundance across gestation for broad and refined cell states. Early-enriched neighbourhoods are SpatialFDR < 0.1 with logFC < 0, late-enriched are SpatialFDR < 0.1 with logFC > 0.

Logistic regression prediction probabilities for a model trained on time-encoded prenatal and adult skin and projected onto skin organoid data — one row per cell, columns per gestational-age bin, for overall cell states and per broad category. The largest file in the bundle (~95 MB, 396,880 rows).

Differential expression within prenatal epidermal cell states by gestational age group (PCW): two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum, BH adjusted. Use for genes that change with developmental time rather than between cell types. Note some gene symbols have been mangled into dates by a spreadsheet (e.g. MARCH1 -> 2024-08-07).
CellRank output: lineage driver genes for the inferred epidermal, fibroblast and endothelial trajectories, as per-lineage correlation with p, q and confidence intervals in repeated column blocks.

Summarised CellPhoneDB ligand-receptor interactions for prenatal skin cell types, split by early (<= 11 PCW) and late (>= 12 PCW) gestation and for skin organoid. Significance is mean receptor-ligand expression p < 0.05 by empirical shuffling, FDR-adjusted.

Genes2Genes trajectory alignment between prenatal skin and skin organoid fibroblasts for all 1,369 transcription factors: alignment similarity percentage and the 5-state alignment string (M match, W compression warp, V expansion warp, I insertion, D deletion).

Logistic regression prediction probabilities for a model trained on human prenatal skin and projected onto murine embryonic skin, at broad (low-resolution) cluster level. One row per murine cell, one column per human broad annotation.

As Supplementary Table 10 but at refined (high-resolution) cell-state level: one row per murine cell, one column per human refined annotation. Use for cross-species correspondence of a specific fine cell state.
Gene mutations implicated in genetic hair diseases found along the inner root sheath, outer root sheath/companion layer and hair fibroblast trajectories, with literature references.
Differential expression comparing prenatal skin fibroblasts against healthy adult skin fibroblasts (Wilcoxon, BH adjusted), as two column blocks.
Gene set enrichment for prenatal skin fibroblasts: Fisher exact test, BH adjusted, ranked by z-score, with the overlapping gene list per term.
Gene set enrichment for healthy adult skin fibroblasts (the legend's title repeats 'prenatal', but the contents are the adult comparison). Same columns as Supplementary Table 14.
Differential expression between Milo-defined early- and late-gestation WNT2+ fibroblasts (Wilcoxon, BH adjusted).
Gene set enrichment for WNT2+ fibroblasts enriched in early gestation (Milo early neighbourhoods).
Gene set enrichment for WNT2+ fibroblasts enriched in late gestation (Milo late neighbourhoods).

Logistic regression probabilities from a model trained on reindeer skin fibroblast classes (antler velvet and back skin) projected onto human prenatal skin fibroblasts grouped by gestational age. One row per cell.
Pro-regenerative and pro-fibrotic gene lists published for reindeer skin (antler velvet and back), from Sinha et al. 2022 (PMID 36493752). Two columns, one gene list each.

Logistic regression probabilities from a model trained on reindeer skin macrophage clusters projected onto human prenatal skin macrophage subsets. One row per cell, carrying the original prenatal macrophage label alongside the predicted reindeer cluster. Column headers for the predicted classes are bare cluster numbers.

Differential expression between prenatal skin macrophage subsets — TLM, iron-recycling, LYVE1+ and MHC-II+ — each computed against the rest of the myeloid cells (Wilcoxon, BH adjusted). The marker table for any of the four macrophage subsets. Laid out as one five-column block per subset, with the subset name in the row above the header.
Gene set enrichment for genes differentially expressed by TLM macrophages (Fisher exact, BH adjusted, ranked by z-score).

Gene set enrichment for genes differentially expressed by iron-recycling macrophages (Fisher exact, BH adjusted, ranked by z-score). The functional-annotation counterpart to that subset's markers in Supplementary Table 22.
Gene set enrichment for genes differentially expressed by LYVE1+ macrophages.
Gene set enrichment for genes differentially expressed by MHC-II+ macrophages.
The angiogenesis gene sets (GO Biological Process 2021) used to compute angiogenesis module scores. Each column is one GO term, listing its genes down the column rather than one row per gene.

tables.description: Summarised CellPhoneDB ligand-receptor interactions across all prenatal skin cell states (not split by gestation, unlike Supplementary Table 8). Significance p < 0.05, FDR-adjusted.
Gene lists used for the endothelial and hypoxia module scores; each column is one score's gene set.
Differential expression between prenatal skin and skin organoid for all cell states, grouped by dataset, as prenatal and organoid column blocks.

A filtered list of genes encoding secreted proteins that differ between prenatal skin and skin organoid, with log fold change and adjusted p-value. Note the discrepancy: the legends document calls this the upregulated list, while the sheet's own title row says downregulated — check the sign of fetal_logfoldchanges before relying on either.

The companion filtered list of secreted-protein genes for the opposite direction to Supplementary Table 31, same columns. Both sheets carry a 'downregulated' title row; use the fold-change sign rather than the label.
Gene set enrichment for the secreted-protein genes upregulated in prenatal skin relative to skin organoid.
Gene set enrichment for the secreted-protein genes downregulated in prenatal skin relative to skin organoid.
NicheNet prioritised ligands, ranked by ligand activity score (auroc, aupr, corrected aupr, pearson, rank).
NicheNet prioritised ligands with their active target genes and interaction weights — one row per ligand-target pair.
NicheNet prioritised ligands against their receptors, filtered to bona fide ligand-receptor interactions. Ligands are columns, receptors are rows.

Antibodies used for immunofluorescence of prenatal skin and skin organoid cryosections: RRID, vendor, catalogue number, clonality, clone, dilution and application. Use it to check what a protein-level claim was stained with.
The database of predicted secreted proteins and their encoding genes, with synonyms, Ensembl and UniProt identifiers, protein class and evidence level.

tables.description: Microenvironment labels used for the spatial analysis, defined by predominant cell-type composition and/or spatial or age distribution. Maps a microenvironment number to its label.

Prose legends for all 40 supplementary tables, one paragraph each: the table's title and what analysis produced it. Read this first — it characterises the whole bundle in ~11,000 characters, and the individual workbooks carry no descriptions of their own.
Source data for Fig. 2b: cell counts per refined annotation, per donor and gestational age. Use for how abundant a prenatal skin cell state is and how that changes across gestation.
Source data for Fig. 4c: cell counts per refined annotation, per donor and gestational age, for the subset shown in that panel.
Source data for Fig. 4i: endothelial density per skin-organoid batch and condition, from image quantification.
Source data for Extended Data Fig. 3c: cell counts per refined annotation, per donor and gestational age.
Source data for Extended Data Fig. 3f: FOXP3+ cell counts in hair-follicle versus non-hair-follicle regions.
Source data for Extended Data Fig. 7g: per-experiment image quantification, laid out as one column block per experiment.
Source data for Extended Data Fig. 8g: per-experiment image quantification, one column block per experiment.
Source data for Extended Data Fig. 10g: timecourse quantification for endothelial-cell-only and co-culture conditions.
Source data for Extended Data Fig. 11i: timecourse quantification for endothelial-cell-only and co-culture conditions.
